candidates.statement: Order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, which the gateway surfaces as 502 on POST /v1/checkout. Traces and logs show every checkout failure paired with a 500 from order within milliseconds, so the fault originates in the order service, not the gateway.
candidates.uncertainty: Root cause inside order (code, dependency, or resource) is not established; only the 500 origin is bounded.

report.explanation: Gateway checkout 502s are consistently caused by order service 500s on POST /v1/orders, seen in traces and logs with matching correlation IDs and short durations. Gateway health endpoints stay 200. The bounded candidate is an order-service HTTP 500 fault; the specific internal cause needs order-side evidence.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces for the failing POST /v1/orders requests to identify the internal error cause
Order service dependency metrics (inventory, payment, postgresql) to rule out downstream latency or db-pool-exhaustion
